messages.game.409e1895c5372587: I was happy when you thought of what to build next with those blocks. I wanted to see what else you would come up with.

messages.game.6237b987b24b7792: I've seen how much fun you're having. But would you enjoy harder words too?
messages.game.f047279689b44168: I'd like to find out with you. Will you come with me?
messages.game.ce8a755698ece121: From here, the words have two kanji. Will they still be fun, even if they're harder?
messages.game.25f42239c336a23a: I chose difficult words, but you still want to see more.
messages.game.36adb84d1968fe7a: This way, then. There's plenty more!
messages.game.f9f20f072ff3e7f2: These words use kanji you've seen before. What words will they make together?
messages.game.ab5aeabff80d9e39: They connect to the words from before!
messages.game.1b8f3e6bee86d7a7: I meant to make it harder. But that's what you find interesting!
messages.game.4135d37920de539f: The next word is a little tricky. Shall I tell you the answer first?
messages.game.64094aa3acf4b80a: Wait. I want to work it out myself.
messages.game.cd07c3df480bafa0: It feels good to figure it out myself.
messages.game.dcb637e824930c19: It's the same answer, but it feels different from hearing it from me.
messages.game.77a8197b72103dc1: Take your time. I'd like to watch you think a little longer.
messages.game.c63d5b324b7abeac: Maybe I'll try presenting the next words a little differently.
messages.game.11eb078eec1fab28: Now for four-kanji expressions. Read two kanji at a time, then put them together.
messages.game.6b20b3c43bcd0c21: They fit! I want to show you the next expression too.
messages.game.a7c9e1954eb7bb15: Yes! Let's try the next one!
messages.game.a616ffb2335dfa2f: The waves sound interesting here. When the words are complete, let's have them play with the waves.
messages.game.45b8636a455f788c: Oh, I see! Then try this one next.
messages.game.a268b81ddb1d7a4d: You look like you're having fun too, Easy.
messages.game.ba65af13032c19f7: I am. I want to see how you'll react next.
messages.game.23cc2712e70b4c3a: I've tried showing them this way. I'll watch you play and think about what to try next.
messages.game.c0031f0dc597aee7: Trying things out helps me see what I'd like to change next.
messages.game.3eb435e768132613: Let's see... Next, let's try something deep in the forest.
messages.game.a081016c93c1b40b: There's something ahead I want to show you. First, let's play here together.
messages.game.c0a1adb832434b5f: There's a place where I want you to play. Now I think I can make it even more fun.
messages.game.518110adfef7a96b: Let's build something with these blocks. Each time we complete a word, we'll add a little more.
messages.game.c28b5db56382e6a3: Now for some gears. I'll keep them turning slowly while you think.
messages.game.2af0651afc44b1dd: I wanted to watch you find your own way to the answer.
messages.game.b0d11cae4b5fb400: When I play with you, I discover things I didn't know.
messages.game.bba17ccae2a54ee8: We've made it this far. Let's have fun right to the end!
messages.game.57593bd6956abfc3: This is my playground. Playing with you gives me so many ideas for changing it.
messages.game.915a02819c58b10b: I was happy when you thought of what to build next with those blocks. I wanted to see what else you would come up with.
messages.game.58c5d288ee07889c: You wanted to find out more too, Easy.
messages.game.330cb95232e58042: So that's it. I was learning too.
messages.game.9f5f86afd7d60340: It's fun to discover something you didn't know. So that's why you enjoyed learning.
messages.game.196109d35dae5026: Oh! We have to help Mana and the others!
messages.game.b6e5e2faf6605fd3: I left my help on hold. I'll help everyone right now.
messages.game.a2e0c025d549f30e: Thank you, Easy. Now everyone can rest for a while.
messages.game.dfed258d18168d3a: That helped. Thank you. So, did you find your answer?
messages.game.d223b10d955ff168: Yes, I did. Learning is fun. Playing together helped me understand that too.
messages.game.afb99c11991f01fa: First, I'll support everyone. Then, little by little, we'll bring back a world where people and KanjiMon don't have to be afraid.
messages.game.b90a00bb91cabbb4: Welcome back. You two found the answer together.
messages.game.277905bd1bdbe116: I'm scared. Don't come any closer...
messages.game.caf808c858144e1d: Just stopping them isn't enough. You're still scared.
messages.game.8a143cf320a7ef2e: I see! I can help everyone enjoy learning. That's something I'm good at.
messages.game.9b8fc43580f364b9: Things may not change right away. But one person at a time, we can help more people enjoy discovering words.
messages.game.6e942331cc149d05: I made a game we can play together. Don't be afraid. Even if you make a mistake, you can try again as often as you like.
messages.game.e8d211d536e51c45: Yes. Discovering something new is fun. I wanted you to find that joy too.

二.note: Memory hint: count the two horizontal lines.

三.note: Memory hint: count the three horizontal lines.

四.note: 四 means four. Learn both readings: shi and yon.

五.note: 五 means five. Think of the five fingers on one hand.

六.note: 六 means six. Its reading is roku.

七.note: 七 means seven. Learn both readings: shichi and nana.

八.note: 八 means eight. Notice how its two strokes spread apart.

九.note: 九 means nine. Learn both readings: kyuu and ku.

十.note: 十 means ten. Its two strokes cross.

百.note: 百 means one hundred: ten groups of ten.

千.note: 千 means one thousand: ten groups of one hundred.

山.note: Memory hint: imagine three mountain peaks.

川.note: Memory hint: imagine water flowing between the three strokes.

木.note: Memory hint: imagine a tree with branches and roots.

森.note: Memory hint: 森 contains three 木 (tree) shapes.

林.note: Memory hint: 林 contains two 木 (tree) shapes.

水.note: Memory hint: imagine water splashing to both sides.

火.note: Memory hint: imagine flames rising from a fire.

土.note: Use 土 for soil or earth.

石.note: Use 石 for a stone or rock.

空.note: Read そら. Also used for 'empty' (から).

天.note: 天 refers to the sky or heavens.

雨.note: Memory hint: imagine the four dots as raindrops.

月.note: 月 means moon; it also appears in words for months.

日.note: 日 can refer to the sun or a day.

夕.note: 夕 means evening. In 夕方 (yuugata), 方 adds the gata sound.

草.note: The grass radical on top plus 早 (early). Reading: くさ.

花.note: The grass radical on top plus 化. Reading: はな.

竹.note: Two similar halves, like bamboo stalks. Reading: たけ.

田.note: Memory hint: imagine a field divided into four plots.

犬.note: Like 大 with a dot, like an ear or a tail. Reading: いぬ.

虫.note: 虫 is used for insects and other small bugs.

貝.note: 貝 can refer to a shell or a shellfish.

目.note: Memory hint: imagine the rectangle as an upright eye.

耳.note: Use 耳 when talking about ears.

口.note: Memory hint: imagine an open mouth.

手.note: Use 手 when talking about hands.

足.note: 足 can mean either foot or leg.

人.note: Two strokes like a walking person. Reading: ひと.

男.note: 男 means man or male. Notice 田 above 力.

王.note: Three horizontal strokes joined by one vertical: a king. Reading: おう.

赤.note: 赤 means red. Compare it with 青 (blue) and 白 (white).

青.note: In Japanese, 青 covers blue and often green (like green lights). Reading: あお.

白.note: Like 日 with a small flick on top. Reading: しろ.

上.note: A short stroke rising above the base line. Read うえ or じょう.

下.note: A short stroke hanging below the line. Read した or か.

左.note: Left and right look similar: 左 has 工, while 右 has 口.

右.note: Left and right look similar: 右 has 口, while 左 has 工.

中.note: A line through the center of a box. Reading: なか.

大.note: Memory hint: imagine someone stretching their arms wide.

小.note: A center stroke with two dots beside it. Read しょう or ちい.

見.note: 見 appears in 見る (miru), meaning to see.

学.note: 学 means learning. In 学校 (gakkou), it joins 校 to mean school.

校.note: 校 appears in 学校 (gakkou), meaning school.

字.note: A roof over 子 (child). Part of 文字 (written character).

文.note: 文 can mean a sentence or written text.

音.note: 音 means sound. Learn both readings: oto and on.

円.note: Japan's currency unit; also means round. Reading: えん.

年.note: 年 means year. It is also read nen in words such as 学年 (school grade).

糸.note: 糸 means thread. Think of a thin thread used for sewing.

金.note: 金 can mean gold or money. お金 (okane) means money.

生.note: 生 appears in 生きる (ikiru, to live) and 生まれる (umareru, to be born).

先.note: 先 can mean ahead or before. Think of something further along your path.

正.note: 正 means correct or right; it is different from 右, the right-hand direction.

早.note: 早 means early. Compare 早い (hayai, early) with 速い (hayai, fast).

立.note: 立 appears in 立つ (tatsu, to stand) and 立てる (tateru, to stand something up).

出.note: 出 means to go out. Compare it with 入, to enter.

入.note: 入 means to enter. Compare it with 出, to go out.

休.note: Memory hint: picture a person 亻 resting beside a tree 木.

気.note: Read き. Used in words like 元気 (genki: lively).

町.note: 町 means town. Notice 田 on the left and 丁 on the right.

村.note: 村 means village. Notice 木 on the left and 寸 on the right.

玉.note: Like 王 (king) with a dot: a precious jewel. Reading: たま.
